text:
Predicates:
InCity(x, y) ::: x is in city y.
InState(x, y) ::: x is in state y.
City(y) ::: y is a city.
State(y) ::: y is a state.
InSameState(x, y) ::: x and y are in the same state.
ExclusiveStates(x, y, z, w) ::: x and y are in one state, z and w are in a different state, with no overlap.
Premises:
City(Billings) ∧ InState(Montana, Montana) ∧ City(Butte) ∧ City(Helena) ∧ City(Missoula) ::: Billings is a city in Montana; Montana includes Butte, Helena, and Missoula.
InCity(WhiteSulphurSprings, Montana) ∧ InCity(Butte, Montana) ::: White Sulphur Springs and Butte are cities in Montana.
InCity(StPierre, NotInMontana) ::: St Pierre is not in Montana.
∀x (InCity(x, Butte) → ¬InCity(x, StPierre)) ::: Any city in Butte is not in St Pierre.
ExclusiveStates(Butte, StPierre, Montana, NotMontana) ::: Butte and St Pierre are in different states; no city belongs to more than one state, except for Bristol, Texarkana, Texhoma, and Union City.
Conclusion:
InSameState(Butte, StPierre) ::: Butte and St Pierre are in the same state.
